title: A humanoid robot spent 11 months at BMW: was it profitable? (what was measured, by whom, against what)
source: physicalai.santismm.com/en/case-studies/bmw-spartanburg-figure-02 and /en/platforms/figure-02 · Figure AI (2025-11-19) · BMW Group (2024-08-06 and 2026-02-27) · Fortune (2025-04-06)

scenes.text: A humanoid robot spent 11 months in a BMW factory. Was it profitable? Nobody has published that.
It was Figure 02. It picked sheet-metal parts and placed them on a welding fixture, in 10-hour shifts.
According to Figure: more than 1,250 hours, 90,000 parts and 30,000 cars.
Its targets: 84 seconds per cycle, over 99% correct cycles and zero interventions. The results? Not published.
And in 2025, its founder talked about a fleet. BMW described a single robot, on a single task.
It's like an odometer: it tells you how far you've driven, not whether you got there sooner or what you spent.
Ask: what was measured, by whom, and against what? Here, Figure gives the numbers and BMW repeats them: level B, no independent verification.
Counting parts is not measuring results.
Save it, and share it with someone who trusts any demo.
